items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: the whites in the neighborhood, like a white boy by the name of Ellis, one by the name of Johnson, one white boy by the name of Washington

ctx.x: We were talking about holidays and things. When you were a kid, what did you do for Mardi Gras? How was Mardi Gras celebrated?

Well, when I was a kid, I would cross. My daddy would bring me to the parades when I was, you know, five, six, seven years of age. But as we moved on this side of the river when my mother and father separated, I started leaving 515 Third Street and walking down Jackson Avenue all the way to St. Charles Avenue and watched the parades. That's what we did. Now on Mardi Gras day, I would mask sometimes as a cowboy, sometimes as whatever. I felt like putting on and just hung out with my classmates, the friends who…
I had a question about Carnival because people, because you're looking at Carnival probably sometime in the 1930s, I guess.
